newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana's Kgolo ya Sechaba to unbundle.
newsitem.headline: Botswana's Kgolo ya Sechaba to unbundle.

text.p: Botswana investment company Kgolo ya Sechaba (KYS) is to seek shareholder approval to unbundle, via a voluntary liquidation, in order to unlock the underlying value of the company's assets.
For some time, the company's shares have been trading at a discount to net asset value (NAV) of around 38 percent.
An extraordinary general meeting has been called for January 22 to consider the move.
Meanwhile the company's shares were suspended at the company's request on the Botswana Stock Exchange from noon on Wednesday and would remain so until a liquidator was appointed.
The company said when it listed in December 1994, the market was buoyant and the stock reflected a discount to NAV of 10.7 percent, but a slide on the BSE saw it rise to 31.2 percent.
"Despite exceding every performance objective specified in its listing statement by a handsome margin, the share price did not respond," the company said.
Kgolo ya Sechaba's attributable income for the year ended September rose to 5.92 million pula compared to 5.86 million pula in the previous 15 months.
The company raised dividends to 16.0 thebe per share compared to 14.5 thebe previously.
In its unbundling announcement, the company lists assets valued at 62.7 million pula and estimates a distribution of 62.5 million pula or 2.1 pula per share.
Shares closed at pula 1.45 pula on December 13.
Announcing results last month, the company said that an offer to purchase all the company's shares had been received, but the price offered and terms of payment were unacceptable.

But it said it was aware of shareholders' concerns about the discount to NAV. It said it was reviewing strategic options which might enhance shareholder wealth, the most obvious of which was placing the company into voluntary liquidation.
KYS's single largest asset is 10.8 million shares in brewery holding company Sechaba valued at 27.5 million pula.
"Interest has already been shown in these shares," the company said.
It added that a 10.3 million pula investment in unlisted Sun International Botswana could be distributed as a dividend if not sold and maybe create a platform for listing on the BSE.

A firm offer had been received to purchase KYS' 2.2 million pula holding in Botswana Insurance at current market price and to negotiate the purhcaase of a 3.5 million pula holding in unlisted insurance company Minet Botswana Limited.

KYS also has shares worth 4.6 million pula in milling company and food wholesaler Sefalana, a 1.5 million pula investment in food and tobacco wholesaler Metsef and a 1.2 million pula investment in oil company Engen.
It also has stakes in Barclays Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, clothing chain Pep and Johannesburg listed Servgro International Ltd.
